\# R Code Chunk in Quarto

\# 1. Load data

data(iris)

set.seed(42)

\# 2. Split data (70% training, 30% test)

train_index \<- sample(nrow(iris), 0.7 \* nrow(iris))

train_data \<- iris\[train_index, \]

test_data \<- iris\[-train_index, \]

\# 3. Save to CSV files

write.csv(train_data, "train.csv", row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(test_data, "test.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("Data split complete. train.csv and test.csv saved.")

\# (b)

\# Python Code Chunk in Quarto (using reticulate's Python engine)

import pandas as pd

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score

\# 1. Read data

train_df = pd.read_csv("train.csv")

test_df = pd.read_csv("test.csv")

\# 2. Prepare data for model

feature_cols = \['Sepal.Length', 'Sepal.Width', 'Petal.Length', 'Petal.Width'\]

X_train = train_df\[feature_cols\]

y_train = train_df\['Species'\]

X_test = test_df\[feature_cols\]

y_test = test_df\['Species'\]

\# 3. Fit Random Forest Model

model = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42)

model.fit(X_train, y_train)

\# 4. Predict on test data

y_pred = model.predict(X_test)

\# 5. Calculate Accuracy (optional for quick check)

accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)

print(f"Random Forest Model Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f}")

\# 6. Store results for R (using r.put)

\# Store true values and predictions back to the R session's main environment

r.true_labels = y_test.tolist()

r.predictions = y_pred.tolist()

\# (c)

\# R Code Chunk in Quarto

library(ggplot2)

library(caret) \# For confusionMatrix

\# 1. Convert lists from Python back to factors/vectors in R

true_labels_R \<- factor(unlist(py\$true_labels))

predictions_R \<- factor(unlist(py\$predictions), levels = levels(true_labels_R)) \# Ensure levels match

\# 2. Calculate Confusion Matrix

conf_matrix \<- confusionMatrix(predictions_R, true_labels_R)

print(conf_matrix)

\# 3. Create data frame for visualization (Hint: scatter plot with dot size proportional to count)

conf_df \<- as.data.frame(conf_matrix\$table)

\# 4. Visualization (Scatter plot with dot size)

ggplot(conf_df, aes(x = Reference, y = Prediction, size = Freq, color = Freq)) +
geom_point() +
scale_size_continuous(range = c(5, 20)) +
scale_color_gradient(low = "yellow", high = "red") +
geom_text(aes(label = Freq), color = "black", size = 4) +
labs(title = "Confusion Matrix Visualization (Test Data)",
x = "True Class (Reference)",
y = "Predicted Class (Prediction)") +
theme_minimal() +
theme(legend.position = "none")
